info.title: Ferry API
info.description:
The HTTP API of [Ferry](https://github.com/Carter2307/ferry), a self-hosted Render alternative. The `ferry` CLI and the web dashboard use exactly this API.

**Authentication.** Every `/api/v1` route needs an API token as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`: one created in the dashboard (Server → Account) or by `ferry login`, or the server token stored in `<data-dir>/api_token`. Use the **Authorize** button to set it here. `GET` requests may pass it as `?access_token=<token>` instead, because browsers' `EventSource` can't set headers (prefer the header: query strings end up in logs). The dashboard itself signs in to the server's account (`POST /api/v1/auth/login`) and is then authenticated by its session cookie; the operations on the account, its sessions and its tokens (`/api/v1/auth/...`) only accept that session. Webhooks (`/hooks/...`) authenticate with their own secrets, and `/healthz`, this document, Swagger UI and the calls made before signing in (the `auth` tag says which) need no token.

**Conventions.** JSON bodies with snake_case fields; request bodies reject unknown fields and an empty body counts as `{}`. `{id}` path segments accept a resource id **or** its name. Errors are `ApiErrorBody` documents (`{"error": {"code", "message"}}`) with the matching HTTP status; unknown `/api` routes are JSON 404s. Boolean query flags accept `true/false`, `1/0`, `yes/no`, `on/off`, and an empty value means `true` (`?follow`).

**Streams.** Logs and the change feed are Server-Sent Events (`text/event-stream`): see the `logs` operations and `GET /api/v1/events`. Idle streams get a `: keep-alive` comment every 15 s, and every stream ends when the server shuts down.

post.description: What `ferry login` calls first. The terminal then shows `code` and opens `/cli-login?id=<id>` of the dashboard, where the signed-in administrator checks the code and approves; meanwhile the terminal polls `POST /api/v1/auth/cli/{id}/token` with `secret`. A request waits 10 minutes, and a restart of the server forgets it. No token needed.

post.description: Checks the email and password of the account and starts a session: the answer sets the session cookie (`HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Strict`; named `ferry_session_<port>` after the port of the address the browser uses, so that servers sharing a host name keep a session each), which authenticates the dashboard's requests from then on. A session ends 30 days after it was last used. After 10 failed attempts in 5 minutes, sign-ins are refused until the oldest is 5 minutes old. No token needed.

401.description: Wrong email or password (code `invalid_credentials`).

post.description: Ends the session of the request's cookie and clears the cookie. Succeeds without a session too.
Needs the dashboard's session and the current password. Every other session of the account ends; this one stays. (A forgotten password is replaced on the server with `ferryd reset-password`.)

400.description: The new password is shorter than 8 characters.

401.description: Not signed in, or the current password is wrong (code `invalid_credentials`).

delete.description: Signs that browser out. Ending the session of this request is signing out. Needs the dashboard's session.

post.description: Only while the server has no account (`setup_required`). `code` is the setup code: `ferryd` prints it in a link (`/setup?code=…`) when it starts without an account, and keeps it in `<data-dir>/setup_code`, so only someone on the server can create the account. The answer signs the browser in (it sets the session cookie). No token needed.

201.description: The account was created and this browser is signed in.

400.description: Invalid email, or a password shorter than 8 characters.

409.description: The server already has an account.

get.summary: Is there an account, and is this request signed in
get.description: What the dashboard asks first. `setup_required` is true while the server has no account: it is then created with `POST /api/v1/auth/setup`. `auth` says how the request is authenticated (`session` for the dashboard's cookie, `token` for an API token), or is `null` when it isn't; credentials that are wrong or expired count as none. No token needed.

The named API tokens, the newest first: their name, the end of the token and when they were last used. Never the tokens themselves. The server token of `<data-dir>/api_token` isn't listed. Needs the dashboard's session.

post.description: Creates or updates the services, datastores and env groups a `ferry.yaml` / `render.yaml` describes (nothing is deleted) and queues the deploys that follow. Send the JSON `ApplyBlueprint` request, or the YAML itself with a YAML content type (`application/yaml`, `text/yaml`) and `?dry_run=`. A dry run only reports the planned actions.

parameters.name: dry_run
parameters.description: Only report what would be done (for raw YAML bodies; JSON bodies can also set `dry_run`).

requestBody.description: The blueprint: a JSON `ApplyBlueprint` request, or raw YAML.

application/yaml.example:
services:
  - type: web
    name: web
    image: nginx:alpine

post.description: Creates the row (`creating`) and provisions the container. A failed provisioning still answers 201, with status `failed` and the reason in `error`. Datastores and services share one namespace of names. `memory_limit_mb` (MiB, 16 MiB to 1 TiB) and `cpu_limit` (CPUs, 0.01 to 512, rounded to 0.01) limit the container; omitted or `0` = the server default (see `GET /api/v1/info`).

patch.description: Every field is optional: `memory_limit_mb` (MiB, 16 MiB to 1 TiB) and `cpu_limit` (CPUs, 0.01 to 512, rounded to 0.01); `0` = back to the server default (see `GET /api/v1/info`). The limits are applied to the datastore's container in place, without a restart, whatever the datastore's status (a memory limit below what the datastore currently uses can fail, or get it killed for running out of memory; a `failed` datastore gets them for its next start). A datastore whose container is not created yet gets them when it is. When applying them fails after they were saved, the error message says so.

get.description: Tells a client what changed so it refetches only that: API writes are reported at once, the engine's own changes (deploy progress, datastore provisioning, cron runs) within about a second.

200.description: Server-Sent Events. First `event: ready` (`data: {}`) once the feed watches the store: changes after it are reported, so (re)fetch your data after `ready`. Then one `event: change` per change, whose `data` is a `ChangeEvent` JSON object `{kind, id, service_id, action}`: `kind` is `service`, `deploy`, `datastore`, `env_group`, `job` or `git_connection`; `action` is `created`, `updated` or `deleted`; `service_id` is set for services (their own id), deploys and jobs, `null` otherwise. A subscriber that falls behind gets `{"kind": "all", "id": "*", "service_id": null, "action": "resync"}` and should refetch everything. `: keep-alive` comments every 15 s; the stream only ends when the server shuts down.

401.description: Missing or invalid API token, or no session.

post.summary: Authorize a git account in the browser
post.description:
Starts connecting an account on the provider's own pages and answers with where to send the browser (`status: redirect`): a URL to navigate to (`method: get`) or to submit a form with `fields` to (`method: post`). When the provider is done it sends the browser back to `redirect_uri` (the dashboard's `/git/callback` page) with query parameters to hand to `POST /api/v1/git/callback`.

**GitHub**: the browser posts a manifest to GitHub, which registers a private GitHub App for this server (on the user's account, or in `organization`) and then asks the account which repositories the app may read. No token is ever typed: the app's key mints short-lived tokens.

**GitLab**: the account authorizes an OAuth application created for this server (scopes `read_api` and `read_repository`, redirect URI = `redirect_uri`). Give its `client_id` and `client_secret` the first time (400 `git_application_required` otherwise); they are kept for later authorizations.

With `connection_id`, resumes a `pending` connection or authorizes a connection again; the answer is `status: connected` when nothing is left to do (a GitHub App that is already installed).

200.description: Where to send the browser, or the connection when it is already complete.

400.description: Invalid `redirect_uri`, `base_url` or organization; a provider that needs its OAuth application first (code `git_application_required`); or the provider refused (code `git_authorization_rejected`).

401.description: Missing or invalid API token, or no session.

502.description: The provider could not be reached, or answered an error (code `git_provider_unavailable`).

get.summary: List the branches of a repository
get.description: The branches of a repository and its default one, asked from the repository's remote itself (`git ls-remote`) on every call. Works for any repository URL a service can deploy from; it is read the way a deploy would clone it: with the git connection that serves the URL when there is one (`connection_id` in the answer), with the credentials the URL carries, or without any.

parameters.name: repo_url
parameters.description:
The repository: any URL a service can deploy from (`https://…`,
`git@host:owner/name.git`, a path on the server).

400.description: Malformed repository URL.

401.description: Missing or invalid API token, or no session.

502.description: The remote refused, wasn't found or didn't answer in time (code `git_remote_unreachable`): the message says why, and what to do when it looks like a private repository.

post.summary: Finish a step of a browser authorization
post.description: Takes the query parameters the provider sent the browser back with (to the `redirect_uri` given to `POST /api/v1/git/authorize`): `state`, and `code` and / or `installation_id`. Answers with the next page to send the browser to (`status: redirect`: after GitHub registered the app, its installation page) or with the connection (`status: connected`). A `state` works once, for an hour. Without `state` but with an `installation_id` (GitHub sends the browser back after an installation was changed on its own pages), the connection of that installation is read again.

200.description: The next step, or the connection.

400.description: Unknown, expired or already used `state`; a missing parameter; or the provider refused: the user denied the authorization, the code is no longer valid (code `git_authorization_rejected`).

401.description: Missing or invalid API token, or no session.

502.description: The provider could not be reached, or answered an error (code `git_provider_unavailable`).

get.description: The GitHub / GitLab accounts this server is authorized to read the repositories of, with the names of the services whose repository each one clones. A `pending` connection was started in the browser and not finished. Secrets are never returned.

401.description: Missing or invalid API token, or no session.

post.summary: Connect a git account with an access token
post.description: The alternative to authorizing in the browser (`POST /api/v1/git/authorize`), for scripts and for instances where no application can be registered: connects the account a personal access token belongs to. Ferry asks the provider who the token is, then stores it. On GitHub use a classic personal access token with the `repo` scope, or a fine-grained one with read access to Contents and Metadata; on GitLab one with the `read_api` and `read_repository` scopes. `base_url` selects a self-hosted instance (GitHub Enterprise Server, GitLab self-managed). An account that is already connected gets the token instead of what it had (200 instead of 201). The token is never returned by the API.

200.description: The account was already connected: it now uses this token.

400.description: Malformed token or `base_url`, or the provider rejected the token (code `git_authorization_rejected`).

401.description: Missing or invalid API token, or no session.

delete.description: Deletes the connection and its secrets. What it authorized stays on the provider until it is removed there: the GitHub App (delete it in GitHub's settings), the OAuth grant or the token. Refused while services' repositories are cloned with it, unless `force=true`: those services keep their repository and are cloned without credentials from then on, which fails for private repositories.

get.description: The repositories the connection can read, asked from the provider on every call, most recently updated first: for a GitHub App the repositories the account allowed it to read (see `manage_url`); otherwise the account's own, its organizations' / groups' and those it collaborates on. At most 1000 are listed (`truncated` says when there are more). Use a repository's `clone_url` as the `repo_url` of a service: it is cloned with this connection.

409.description: The connection is pending, or the provider no longer accepts its authorization: an expired or revoked token, an uninstalled app (code `git_authorization_rejected`). Connect the account again.

post.description: Queues a deploy of the service's configured source. The URL (`deploy_hook_path` of the service) is the secret: no token needed. Rotate it with `POST /api/v1/services/{id}/deploy-hook/rotate`.

parameters.name: service_id
parameters.description: The service's **id** (names are not accepted: they are guessable).

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: The service's deploy hook key (part of its `deploy_hook_path`).

202.description: A deploy (trigger `deploy_hook`) was queued; credentials are redacted.

400.description: The service has no source to deploy.

401.description: Unknown service or wrong key (the same answer for both).

409.description: The service is suspended or being deleted.

post.description: Set it up in GitHub with the server's webhook secret (`github_webhook_secret`). A `push` deploys (trigger `webhook`, commit = `after`) every auto-deploy service whose repository and branch match; `ping` answers `{"ok": true}`; other events are ignored. Replayed deliveries (same body or delivery id) are ignored too.

parameters.name: X-Hub-Signature-256
parameters.description: `sha256=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body>` with the webhook secret.

requestBody.description: The event payload: JSON, or form-encoded with the JSON in a `payload` field (GitHub's default content type). At most 25 MiB.

400.description: Invalid payload.

401.description: Missing or invalid signature.

404.description: GitHub webhooks are not enabled (no webhook secret configured).

ApiTokenView.description: A named API token. The token itself is only in the answer that creates it.

hint.description: The last characters of the token.

ApplyBlueprint.description:
`POST /api/v1/blueprints/apply` (JSON body) — or send the raw YAML with
`Content-Type: application/yaml` and `?dry_run=true`.

AuthStatus.description:
`GET /api/v1/auth/status` — what the dashboard needs to know before
anything else: is there an account, and is this browser signed in.

oneOf.description: How this request is authenticated; `null` when it isn't.

setup_required.description:
The server has no account yet: it must be created first
(`POST /api/v1/auth/setup`).

oneOf.description: The account, for a request with a session.

AuthorizeGit.description:
`POST /api/v1/git/authorize` — start, or resume, the authorization of a
git provider account in the browser.

base_url.description:
Web URL of a self-hosted instance (GitHub Enterprise Server, GitLab
self-managed), e.g. `https://gitlab.example.com`. Default:
`https://github.com` / `https://gitlab.com`.

client_id.description:
GitLab: the Application ID of the OAuth application created for
this server. Needed the first time (and to replace the application).

connection_id.description:
Resume the authorization of this (pending) connection, or authorize
it again.

organization.description:
GitHub: register the app in this organization instead of the
user's own account, to reach the organization's repositories.

oneOf.description: The provider to authorize. Not needed with `connection_id`.

redirect_uri.description:
Where the provider sends the browser back when it is done: the
dashboard's `/git/callback` page, which hands the query parameters
it receives to `POST /api/v1/git/callback`.

BlueprintAction.description: One planned/performed change of a blueprint apply.

ChangeEvent.description: One change: the `data` of an `event: change` frame.

id.description: Id of the changed resource (`*` with `resync`).

service_id.description: Set for services (their own id), deploys and jobs (their service); `null` otherwise.

ChangeKind.description: What a change event is about (`all` only with `resync`).

secret.description: The `secret` of the answer that started the request.

token.description: The API token, once: with `approved`, the first time it is collected.

code.description:
Shown by the terminal and by the approval page: the person approving
checks that both match.

id.description: Names the request: the approval page is `/cli-login?id=<id>` of the dashboard.

interval.description: Seconds to wait between two polls.

secret.description: What the terminal collects the token with. It is never shown.

ConnectGit.description:
`POST /api/v1/git/connections` — connect an account of a git provider
with a personal access token (instead of authorizing it in the browser).

base_url.description:
Web URL of a self-hosted instance (GitHub Enterprise Server, GitLab
self-managed), e.g. `https://gitlab.example.com`. Default:
`https://github.com` / `https://gitlab.com`.

token.description:
A personal access token of the account: on GitHub a classic token
with the `repo` scope (or a fine-grained one with read access to
Contents and Metadata), on GitLab one with the `read_api` and
`read_repository` scopes.

expires_in_days.description: Days until the token expires (1 to 3650). Default: it doesn't.

name.description: What the token is for, e.g. `CI` or `laptop` (1 to 100 characters).

cpu_limit.description: CPU limit, in CPUs. Omitted or 0 = the server default.

memory_limit_mb.description: Memory limit, in MiB. Omitted or 0 = the server default.

cpu_limit.description: CPU limit per instance, in CPUs. Omitted or 0 = the server default.

deploy.description: Queue a first deploy (default: true when repo_url or image is set).

env_groups.description: Env groups to link (ids or names).

memory_limit_mb.description: Memory limit per instance, in MiB. Omitted or 0 = the server default.

CreatedApiToken.description: Answer of `POST /api/v1/auth/tokens`: the only time the token is shown.

token.description:
The token, to send as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Keep it: the
server only stores its digest.

Datastore.description: A managed Postgres or Redis instance (one container + one volume).

cpu_limit.description:
CPU limit of the container, in CPUs. `None` = the server default
(`ferryd --default-cpu-limit`).

host_port.description: Port published on the host for external access (bound to 127.0.0.1).

memory_limit_mb.description:
Memory limit of the container, in MiB. `None` = the server default
(`ferryd --default-memory-limit`).

name.description: Unique DNS-label name; also the private-network hostname.

version.description: Major version / image tag, e.g. "16" (postgres) or "7" (redis).

external_url.description: Connection string from the Ferry host (published on 127.0.0.1).

internal_url.description: Connection string on the private network (use from services).

DatastoreView.description: A datastore with its connection info.

Deploy.description: One attempt to ship a version of a service.

image.description: Image that was built / pulled / reused. Set once the build succeeds.

port.description:
Container port this deploy's instances listen on (chosen at deploy time
via `env::choose_port`; None for workers / cron jobs).

oneOf.description: Clone `repo_url` at `branch` (or the exact `commit`) and build.
Build from an uploaded `.tar.gz` stored at `path` on the server.
Pull and run a prebuilt image.
Reuse an already-built local image (rollback / restart / env change).

DeploySource.description: Where a deploy's code / image comes from.

EnvGroup.description: A named, reusable set of environment variables linked to services.

EnvGroupView.description: An env group with its variables and linked services.

EnvVar.description:
A plain environment variable. Values may contain references such as
`${{datastore.db.connectionString}}` (see [`crate::env`]).

GitAuthorization.description:
The next step of a browser authorization (`POST /api/v1/git/authorize`
and `POST /api/v1/git/callback`).

fields.description: `redirect` with `post`: the fields of the form to submit.

url.description: `redirect`: the provider's page to send the browser to.

GitAuthorizationStatus.description: What a browser authorization needs next.

GitBranches.description:
`GET /api/v1/git/branches?repo_url=` — the branches of a repository, as
its remote lists them.

branches.description:
Every branch: the default one first, then by name. Empty for a
repository without commits.

connection_id.description:
Id of the git connection the repository was read with; `null` when
it was read without one.

default_branch.description: The branch the repository's `HEAD` points to, when it says.

GitCallback.description:
`POST /api/v1/git/callback` — the query parameters the provider sent the
browser back with.

error.description:
The `error` parameter, when the provider reports one (the user
refused, the application is misconfigured).

state.description: The `state` parameter: names the authorization this answers.

GitConnectionStatus.description: Whether a git connection can be used.

GitConnectionView.description:
A git connection as returned by the API. Its secrets (tokens, an app's
private key and client secret) are never returned.

account.description:
Login of the account. Empty while an OAuth application waits for
its first authorization.

account_name.description: Display name of the account, if it has one.

base_url.description: Web URL of the provider instance, e.g. `https://github.com`.

client_id.description: Id of the OAuth application or GitHub App (not a secret).

manage_url.description: GitHub App: where the account chooses the repositories it may read.

repository_selection.description: GitHub App: `all` or `selected` repositories of the account.

scopes.description: Scopes of the token, when the provider reports them (empty otherwise).

services.description:
Names of the services whose repository is cloned with this
connection.

token_expires_at.description:
When a personal access token expires, when the provider reports it.
`null` for the other kinds: their tokens are renewed.

token_hint.description:
The end of a personal access token (`…a1b2`), to tell tokens apart.
`null` for the other kinds.

GitRedirectMethod.description: How the browser is sent to the provider.

GitRepository.description: A repository a git connection can access.

clone_url.description: The https clone URL: use it as a service's `repo_url`.

id.description: The provider's id of the repository.

owner.description: The user, organization or group that owns it.

web_url.description: The repository's page on the provider.

truncated.description:
The account can access more repositories than listed (the listing
stops at 1000).

GithubHookResponse.description:
Response of `POST /hooks/github`: `{"deploys": [...]}` for a push,
`{"deploys": [], "ignored": true, "reason": "..."}` for an already
processed delivery, `{"ok": true}` for `ping` and `{"ignored": true}` for
other events.

deploys.description: Deploys queued by a push (credentials redacted).

ignored.description: The delivery wasn't acted on (not a push, or a replayed push).

InstanceStatus.description: Live container state of one instance.

cpu_limit.description: The container's CPU limit (CPUs); `None` when unlimited.

exit_code.description: Exit code of the last exit, for exited / restarting containers.

memory_limit_bytes.description: The container's memory limit (bytes); `None` when unlimited.

oom_killed.description:
The kernel killed the container's process for exceeding its memory
limit (the last time it exited).

state.description: Docker state: created, running, restarting, exited, dead...

JobRun.description: A cron-job run or one-off job (`ferry run`).

command.description: Command override (`sh -c`), else the service start command / image CMD.

instance.description: Short container/instance identifier for runtime logs (None for build logs).

LogStreamKind.description: Which output a line came from.

command.description: Shell command (`sh -c`). Required for non-cron services.

default_cpu_limit.description: CPU limit (CPUs) of containers that set none. 0 = unlimited.

default_memory_limit_mb.description: Memory limit (MiB) of containers that set none. 0 = unlimited.

docker_cpus.description: CPUs of the Docker host, if known.

docker_memory_bytes.description: Total memory of the Docker host (bytes), if known.

auto_deploy.description: Redeploy automatically on git push to `branch`.

branch.description: Branch to build and to watch for auto-deploys.

build_command.description: Build command for native runtimes (e.g. `npm run build`).

cpu_limit.description:
CPU limit of each instance (and of the service's jobs), in CPUs
(`0.5` = half a core). `None` = the server default
(`ferryd --default-cpu-limit`). Takes effect with the next deploy or
restart.

custom_domains.description: Extra hostnames routed to this service (web services and static sites).

disk_mount_path.description:
Persistent volume mount path. A service with a disk uses recreate
(stop-then-start) deploys and is limited to one instance.

health_check_path.description: HTTP path that must answer 2xx/3xx before a new deploy receives traffic.

live_deploy_id.description: The deploy currently live, if any.

memory_limit_mb.description:
Memory limit of each instance (and of the service's jobs), in MiB.
`None` = the server default (`ferryd --default-memory-limit`). Takes
effect with the next deploy or restart.

name.description: Unique DNS-label name; also the private-network hostname.

port.description: Container port the app listens on. `None` = auto (see `env::choose_port`).

publish_dir.description: Directory of built files to serve (static sites).

repo_url.description: Git URL (https, ssh, or local path / file://). Mutually exclusive with `image`.

root_dir.description: Subdirectory of the repo used as build context (monorepos).

schedule.description: 5-field cron expression (cron jobs only), evaluated in UTC.

start_command.description: Start command; overrides the image CMD (run via `sh -c`).

deploy_hook_path.description: `POST` here (no auth header needed) to trigger a deploy.

env_groups.description: Names of linked env groups, in link order.

hosts.description: All hostnames routed to the service.

internal_host.description: Hostname on the private network (= name).

internal_port.description: Port of the live deploy (private network), if known.

url.description: Public URL (web services and static sites).

ServiceView.description: A service as returned by the API (the stored row plus computed fields).

SessionView.description: A browser signed in to the dashboard.

expires_at.description: A session ends 30 days after it was last used.

user_agent.description: The browser, as it named itself when it signed in.

SetupAccount.description:
`POST /api/v1/auth/setup` — create the administrator's account of a
server that has none.

code.description:
The setup code: the `code` of the link `ferryd` prints while the
server has no account (also in `<data-dir>/setup_code`).

SourceArchive.description: A gzip-compressed tar archive of the source tree (`.tar.gz`, at most 512 MiB).

SourceKind.description: Where a service's code comes from (derived from its fields).

StartCliLogin.description: `POST /api/v1/auth/cli` — a terminal asks to be connected (`ferry login`).

name.description:
Who asks, e.g. `ada@laptop`: shown on the approval page, and the name
of the API token that approving creates.

UpdateDatastore.description:
`PATCH /api/v1/datastores/{id}` — change resource limits. 0 clears
(server default). Applied to the running container in place (no restart).

cpu_limit.description: CPU limit, in CPUs. 0 clears (server default); omitted keeps it.

memory_limit_mb.description: Memory limit, in MiB. 0 clears (server default); omitted keeps it.

UpdateService.description:
`PATCH /api/v1/services/{id}` — every field optional. For optional string
settings, an empty string clears the value. Changing `instances` scales,
`suspended` suspends/resumes, `custom_domains` refreshes routes; build
settings and resource limits take effect on the next deploy.

cpu_limit.description:
CPU limit per instance, in CPUs. 0 clears (server default). Takes
effect with the next deploy or restart.

memory_limit_mb.description:
Memory limit per instance, in MiB. 0 clears (server default). Takes
effect with the next deploy or restart.

UserView.description: The account the dashboard is signed in to.

bearer.description: An API token: one created in the dashboard or by `ferry login`, or the server token stored in `<data-dir>/api_token`. `GET` requests may send it as `?access_token=` instead.

session.name: ferry_session
session.description: The dashboard's session: the cookie `POST /api/v1/auth/login` sets, named `ferry_session` followed by the port of the address the browser uses (`ferry_session_7878`). A request that changes something must also come from the dashboard's own origin.

tags.name: info
tags.description: Server info, liveness and this document.

tags.name: auth
tags.description: The account of the server (its administrator), signing in and out of the dashboard, the sessions and the API tokens, and `ferry login` (a terminal asks, the dashboard approves). The status, the first-run setup, signing in and out, and the two calls of a terminal need no authentication; the others only accept the dashboard's session, never an API token.

tags.name: services
tags.description: Web services, private services, background workers, static sites and cron jobs: CRUD, lifecycle actions (restart, suspend, resume, scale, rollback), status and runtime logs.

tags.name: deploys
tags.description: Deploy history, manual deploys, source uploads (`ferry up`), cancellation and build logs.

tags.name: env
tags.description: A service's own environment variables. `?restart=true` restarts the live service when its effective environment changed.

tags.name: env-groups
tags.description: Shared variable sets linked to services (a service's own variables win over its groups'), and linking / unlinking them.

tags.name: domains
tags.description: Custom domains of web services and static sites (unique across services).

tags.name: jobs
tags.description: Job runs: cron runs and one-off commands, with their logs.

tags.name: datastores
tags.description: Managed Postgres and Redis instances with their connection strings and resource limits.

tags.name: git
tags.description: Git connections: the GitHub / GitLab accounts this server is authorized to read the repositories of, to pick a repository and a branch from a list and to clone private repositories. An account is authorized in the browser (a GitHub App on GitHub, an OAuth application on GitLab) or with an access token. Connections belong to the server, not to a service: a repository is cloned with the connection that serves its URL.

tags.name: blueprints
tags.description: Infrastructure as code: apply a `ferry.yaml` / `render.yaml` (idempotent, with a dry run).

tags.name: events
tags.description: The change feed (Server-Sent Events) the web client uses to stay current without polling.

tags.name: hooks
tags.description: Webhooks: secret deploy hook URLs and GitHub push events. They authenticate with their own secrets, never the API token.
